listing.name: Dino Crisis 2 / Alexbeav PSXRecomp
listing.summary: Native Dino Crisis 2 PlayStation recompilation from Alexbeav’s PSXRecomp project.

steps.title: Choose setup for your platform
steps.instruction: On Windows or Linux, use Portcove’s managed setup and select your matching CHD and retail SCPH-1001 BIOS. On a Mac, install a C/C++ compiler, CMake, Ninja and Python 3, then unpack the official ZIP for your Mac into a separate writable folder.

steps.title: Supply your original files on Mac
steps.instruction: Use your own Dino Crisis 2 (USA) disc (SLUS-01279) with its CUE and both BIN tracks in order. The reviewed v0.1.3 Mac kit requires your own retail SCPH-1001 (USA) BIOS. Follow README-SETUP.txt for the requirements of the kit you downloaded.

steps.title: Build and add the prepared Mac player
steps.instruction: Run Dino_Crisis_2_Recompiled from the unpacked folder and follow the Generate & rebuild wizard. In Portcove, select build-release/Dino_Crisis_2_Recompiled and use build-release as the start folder. Leave arguments empty and choose Play after you review the registration.

references.title: Updates and backups
references.instruction: For the upstream Mac route, keep the complete working copy, original disc files, BIOS, saves and settings. Follow upstream instructions for replacement and keep a copy of the runtime that created your saves. Removing the Portcove registration preserves the external files.

presentation.manual_preparation: Provide your own matching two-track CHD for Dino Crisis 2 SLUS-01279 (USA) and legally obtained retail SCPH-1001 BIOS. A copy built with the SCPH-5552 BIOS keeps it until you update; the update needs your SCPH-1001 BIOS. Preserve both disc tracks. Portcove verifies the first data track and track count; the audio track digest and complete TOC are not independently authenticated. OpenBIOS is not an accepted substitute. Managed preparation uses the registered Python/build toolchain and Play skips the setup launcher. Generation, runtime, audio, saves, lifecycle and gameplay are untested. Preserve framework PolyForm Noncommercial and UI MIT notices; no rights to retail game data or generated retail content are inferred. Linux x86-64 uses the pinned managed build toolchain and does not launch the packaged setup host. That standalone host requires GLIBC 2.29, GLIBCXX 3.4.26 and OpenGL; generated-game minimum-host compatibility and Linux runtime behavior remain untested.
